newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN BONDS TO STAY IN GRIP OF YEAR-END LETHARGY.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN BONDS TO STAY IN GRIP OF YEAR-END LETHARGY.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds, which ended a quiet day with pares loses on Monday, are expected to remain rangebound for the foreseeable future as end-of-year lethargy strengthens its grip, traders said.
"I am afraid we may have this kind of market to the end of the year," one trader said.

Traders said there was little or no impact from the monthly OLO auction where the Belgian Treasury accepted bids for a skimpy 15.7 billion francs worth of bonds -- 7.6 billion francs for the March 2001 and 8.1 billion francs for the March 2007.
Traders said the wrangling over the weekend as the lira was grudgingly re-admitted to the European Union's Exchange Rate Mechanism had little immediate impact on the bond markets.

However, they said the two days of arguments that forced EU monetary officials to call in their finance ministers to settle the re-entry rate did give a signal to money markets that there would be no soft options for countries bidding to join the bloc's future single currency.
"That is a very important signal. It shows that countries that have tried to manipulate their figures will not be allowed to get away with it," one trader said.

Traders said the short-term impact of this would be limited, but they warned that it could affect longer-maturity bonds as the 1998 deadline for qualifying for the single currency, due to be introduced in 1999, neared.
"There could be pressure on the long end," one trader said.
Traders said there was otherwise little on the horizon to change the underlying bullish tone of bond markets, with a light correction possible before new buying emerged in the New Year.
The benchmark 2006 OLO yielded 5.98 percent, up from Friday's 5.97. The spread over Bunds widended to 18 basis points from 17.
The December futures contract ended 10 basis points lower at 120.27.
